SMTO-SKL-0172 — GitHub's branch rules blocked this merge

GUID: 21efaa88-4d46-5902-b576-410657ee8258
Slug: github-branch-protection-blocked
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub refused to merge this pull request because the target branch has rules that aren't met yet, such as required reviews or passing checks. Nothing was merged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the pull request on github.com and scroll to the merge box at the bottom. It lists what is still missing, such as an approval or a failing check. GitHub only names the exact rule there; SMTO just knows a branch rule blocked the merge.
  2. Get the missing item done: ask a reviewer to approve, wait for checks to finish and pass, or fix the failing check. The merge stays blocked until every rule on the branch is satisfied.
  3. Ask the Agent to look at the pull request again and then merge it. The Agent must confirm the pull request hasn't changed since it was checked, so it merges exactly what you reviewed.

What success looks like

  • The pull request shows as Merged on github.com and the Agent reports the merge was applied.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the GitHub project's branch rules. Don't ask them to turn off the rules just to get the merge through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub refused the pull request merge with a 403 whose message cites branch protection or a required rule, so SMTO classified it as branch_protection_blocked; nothing was merged.

What this means

  • Merge receives HTTP 403 whose message contains protected/required-rule evidence and is classified as branch_protection_blocked. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Merge receives HTTP 403 whose message contains protected/required-rule evidence and is classified as branch_protection_blocked.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual repository rule, check and review state rather than bypassing the denial.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the target branch's protection rules or rulesets on GitHub and satisfy them (required approvals, status checks, signed commits, linear history, etc.). Then re-read the pull request with github.pull_request, confirm the head SHA is unchanged, and request a new merge with that exact expected_head_sha; SMTO never bypasses branch protection.
  • Satisfy the repository branch rules and required checks/reviews, then inspect the same PR head before requesting a new merge.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Required conditions are satisfied for the exact current PR head.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.
